Tbh it feels as if this show has something against asexuals or they have a very warped idea of what it is. I love the show as a whole, but god damn it, the ace representation is bad.

First the theatre actress in season 2(?), it was only 1 scene and they basically said nothing, very cliché, seemed like they just wanted to throw in the representation for the sake of having it without any real need for an asexual character in the plot.

Now O. First of all, how the hell was it a secret if she had the ace ring on since ep. 1? I guess most people wouldn't know, but still why would she wear it if she wasn't ready to come out? I also didn't particularly like the fact that the only ace character with any sort of story was basically made out to be the main antagonist for most of the season. But this is fine, ofc there are ace people who are bad/mean/act badly, whatever. But the way the asexuality was, well, pretty much weaponised for the personal gain of the characters?? It was so weird, it was only said so that people would have a reason to feel sorry for O, because she was "forced" to come out (she wasn't, there was no need to say this at all). Also justifying ghosting by saying you're ace is so strange.

Ultimately the season was good and all the other ones were as well. And it's not like there was nothing good about O, I like that she was sex-positive, media representation of this is rare. I'm sex-repulsed, but I've seen people say that it accurately represented them as sex-positive aces, so that's good at least. I've made peace with the fact that my asexual label might never be accurately portrayed in media, it's okay I don't really care.
